sections.title: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) Clinical Presentation
sections.content: A1: Image of an old man/lady showing left temporal upper lid swelling with hyperemia and ulceration, temporal mild lower lid hyperemia and swelling associated with temporal upper lid ptosis. In addition, there is temporal eyebrow hair loss with temporal periocular skin hyperpigmentation.

sections.title: Management Strategy for Malignant Eyelid Lesions
content: Diagnostic Workup: Confirmatory incisional biopsy with adequate margin for histopathology.
Primary Treatment: Surgical excision is first-line.
Alternative Treatments: Radiation therapy is the second-best treatment. Topical imiquimod and topical/injectable interferon for non-surgical elderly patients.
Systemic/Regional Workup: Referral to oncologist/internist. SCC/SGC/Melanoma: CT/MRI of brain/orbit (check infiltration of lacrimal gland or perineural invasion). Check sentinel lymph nodes.
Surgical Clearance: Conventional paraffin-embedded, standard frozen section, or Mohs micrographic surgery (lowest recurrence 1%).
Margins: Small BCC (2-4 mm). Large BCC, SCC, SGC, Melanoma (5 mm wide margins).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Management Notes
content: Sebaceous Cell CA (SGC): Perform wide excision (5mm). Send fresh tissue for Oil Red O stain.
Conjunctival Map Biopsy: Perform in SGC (4 bulbar quadrants + medial/lateral tarsal). If positive, use adjunctive cryotherapy.
Imaging: CT orbits/MRI with contrast for infraorbital/intracranial spread in SCC, SGC, and malignant melanoma. For BCC, only if medial canthal lesion.
Medial Canthal BCC: Higher risk of lacrimal sac/orbital involvement. If extended: Radiotherapy or Hedgehog pathway inhibitors (vismodegib).

sections.title: Incomplete Excision Protocol
content: If excisional biopsy shows incomplete margins: Re-excise additional tissue to confirm clearance.
Proceed to eyelid reconstruction only after histopathological confirmation of clean margins.
